request: How much have first-of-class Navy ships overrun their cost estimates?

reply.reply:
The reports reviewed do not establish a single quantified overrun for first-of-class Navy ships: they give lead-ship costs, but not the comparable baseline-to-final figures needed to calculate the overrun. The newest example reviewed is the Constellation lead ship’s FY2026 estimated procurement cost of $1,499.3 million (CRS R44972, PDF p. 10). For comparison, the report gives CVN-78’s final procurement cost as $13,316.5 million in then-year dollars, but the passages reviewed do not quantify its overrun against the FY2008 estimate (CRS RS20643, PDF pp. 7, 12).

[View the evidence brief](output/briefs/case-20261025-150314-4aad.html)
reply.reasoning: Verified sources provide two useful first-of-class cost figures but no directly comparable original estimates and final costs, so an actual overrun amount cannot be established from the passages reviewed.
